definitions.explanation: A tall wooden or concrete pole used to support overhead power lines and telephone cables. A common feature of Japanese streets and neighborhoods.

examples.japanese: {電柱|でんちゅう}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{車|くるま}→車：00516_kuruma⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦ぶつかった→ぶつかる：02412_butsukaru⟧。
examples.english: A car crashed into a utility pole.

examples.japanese: ⟦この→この：00962_kono⟧⟦{通|とお}り→通り：01475_toori⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{電柱|でんちゅう}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{多|おお}すぎる。
examples.english: There are too many utility poles on this street.

examples.japanese: ⟦{市|し}→市：01599_shi⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{景観|けいかん}→景観：12976_keikan⟧⟦{改善|かいぜん}→改善：00144_kaizen⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦ため→ため：01145_tame⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{電柱|でんちゅう}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{地中化|ちちゅうか}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{進|すす}めている→進める：01949_susumeru⟧。
examples.english: The city is promoting the undergrounding of utility poles to improve the landscape.

notes:
USAGE:
Utility poles are a distinctive feature of Japanese cityscapes. In recent years, there has been a movement to bury power lines underground ({無電柱化|むでんちゅうか} or {電柱|でんちゅう}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{地中化|ちちゅうか}) to improve aesthetics and disaster resilience. The word covers both power poles and telephone poles.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {電柱|でんちゅう}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{地中化|ちちゅうか} (undergrounding of utility poles)
- {電柱|でんちゅう}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦ぶつかる→ぶつかる：02412_butsukaru⟧ (to crash into a pole)
- {電柱|でんちゅう}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{立|た}つ→立つ：00758_tatsu⟧ (a pole stands)
